title: Variational Multi-Gaussian Quantum Trajectories
abstract: We propose a variational framework for the efficient simulation of stochastic quantum dynamics in interacting bosonic systems. Our method generalizes the time-dependent variational principle to accommodate quantum state diffusion processes and is tailored for describing quantum trajectories unraveled from a master equation. We adopt a wavefunction ansatz composed of a coherent superposition of Gaussian wavepackets, which allows the fully analytical assembly of the variational equations of motion while capturing both the quantum trajectory dynamics and the Lindblad evolution beyond semiclassical approximations. The method is carefully benchmarked on a Bose-Hubbard dimer, and applied to extended Bose-Hubbard lattices in both 1D and 2D. In particular, we show the emergence of a symmetry-breaking phase transition in 2D lattices, which is absent in 1D chains.
summary: The authors propose a Variational Multi-Gaussian Quantum Trajectory method (sVMG) to simulate open quantum systems governed by a master equation. By projecting the dynamics onto a Gaussian superposition ansatz, they analytically solve the variational equations. The method successfully predicts a dimension-dependent symmetry-breaking phase transition in 2D Bose-Hubbard lattices, validating its utility for studying non-equilibrium quantum criticality.
main_problem: The paper addresses the efficient simulation of stochastic quantum dynamics in interacting bosonic systems, particularly focusing on quantum trajectories derived from a master equation.
main_result: The variational method successfully captures the emergence of a symmetry-breaking phase transition in 2D Bose-Hubbard lattices, a feature absent in 1D chains, demonstrating dimension-dependent criticality.
method: A stochastic time-dependent variational principle (sTDVP) is employed, utilizing a wavefunction ansatz composed of a coherent superposition of Gaussian wavepackets to analytically solve the variational equations of motion.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using interacting bosonic systems, specifically the Bose-Hubbard model, studied on dimers and extended lattices in 1D and 2D. Dynamics are governed by a Lindblad master equation incorporating single-body loss.
key_observables: Antibonding mode population ($\langle \hat{n}_\pi angle$) and bipartite Rényi-2 entanglement entropy ($S_2$).
important_parameters: The study explores different lattice dimensions (1D vs 2D) and varying coupling/interaction parameters relative to the dissipation rate ($\gamma$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on approximating the quantum state using a finite superposition of Gaussian wavepackets ($N_c$), and the analytical tractability stems from the Gaussian structure allowing the evaluation of the quantum geometric tensor.
figures_summary: Figure 2 compares the calculated $\langle \hat{n}_\pi angle$ and $S_2$ for the Bose-Hubbard dimer against exact solutions and other approximations. Figure 3 shows single-trajectory expectation values for 1D and 2D lattices, highlighting the 2D checkerboard pattern.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the sTDVP framework and the multi-Gaussian ansatz. It then benchmarks the method on a Bose-Hubbard dimer, demonstrating accuracy. Finally, it applies the method to 1D and 2D lattices to study phase transitions and compare results across dimensions.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, analytically tractable tool (sVMG) to simulate non-equilibrium quantum dynamics in many-body systems, allowing for the study of complex phenomena like quantum phase transitions beyond standard semiclassical limits.
